documents.title: LUNA-FM: a subword foundation model for long non-coding RNAs for functional inference.
documents.abstract: RNA foundation models (FMs) have shown promise for RNA identification and functional annotation. However, many use single-nucleotide tokenization, which produces long input sequences and can increase computational costs when modelling long RNAs, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). To address these limitations, we introduce LUNA-FM (Length-efficient sUbword-based Nucleic Acid Foundation Model), an RNA language model pretrained on approximately 28 million redundancy-filtered ncRNA sequences. LUNA-FM combines subword tokenization with a long context transformer, enabling efficient modelling

documents.title: Association of Estimated Insulin Sensitivity With Cardiovascular Disease in Individuals Without Diabetes: Use of Traditional and Machine Learning.
documents.abstract: The predictive role of the Estimated Insulin Sensitivity (e-IS) index, serving as a surrogate marker for insulin resistance, in cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mechanisms remains underexplored in nondiabetic populations. We aimed to evaluate the association of e-IS with CVD incidence and its predictive utility for CVD risk.

documents.title: Natural Language Processing Supported by Annotation Process Artifacts to Detect Risky Alcohol Use in Electronic Health Records: Algorithm Development and Validation Study.
documents.abstract: High-risk alcohol use and alcohol use disorder (AUD) are significant contributors to surgical risk and complications yet remain underidentified in surgical populations. While electronic health records (EHRs) contain relevant information about patients' alcohol use in clinical notes, manual chart review is time-intensive and impractical at scale. Natural language processing (NLP) offers a path to automated identification, but alcohol-related risk classes are highly imbalanced in clinical populations, making multiclass classification particularly challenging.

documents.title: RNAcomp2D: a web tool to execute multiple methods and visually compare predictions of RNA secondary structure.
documents.abstract: Ribonucleic acids (RNAs) are involved in many important biological processes. In particular, non-coding RNAs are crucial regulators of cellular processes, playing a significant role in gene expression. RNA secondary structure is key to infer their specific function and for understanding how they interact with other molecules. Many computational models have been developed in the last decade to predict the secondary structure, achieving increasingly higher success rates. However, each new method has its own input-output interface, programming language, computational requirements and, sometimes,

documents.title: Phenotypic expansion of TUBGCP6 primary microcephaly: severe cortical malformations without chorioretinopathy and insights into variant interpretation.
documents.abstract: Biallelic variants of TUBGCP6 are associated with primary microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, short stature, and intellectual disability (ID). Most reported cases had at least one loss-of-function variant.

documents.title: Enhanced prognosis stratification following surgery for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma to optimize clinical decisions by reflecting tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment.
documents.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has an extremely dismal postoperative prognosis. Conventional TNM staging cannot adequately characterize tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment, leading to suboptimal risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an integrated prognostic system for PDAC by combining deep learning (DL)-based radiomic features with guideline‑recommended clinicopathological variables.

documents.title: Intra-DNA k-mer conservation patterns encode evolutionary selection of variants.
documents.abstract: Current approaches to variant effect prediction center on protein function and interspecies conservation, largely ignoring cues embedded in local nucleotide composition. We developed kGain, a metric that quantifies how a point mutation reshapes oligonucleotide frequency relative to the host genome. In Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae long-term evolution data, fixed, essential-gene, and recurrent mutations carry elevated kGain values that grow more pronounced over successive generations. Parallel trends appear in SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and in a bottleneck resistance experim

documents.title: DNNGP-Pro: A multi-omics data integration platform for predictive modeling of complex traits and crop hybrid breeding.
documents.abstract: Accurate prediction of complex agronomic traits poses a long-standing challenge for hybrid crop breeding, which may be resolved by integrating multi-omics data with shared-parent relationship information among hybrids. To accelerate variety development, we constructed the DNNGP-Pro platform for predictive modeling of complex hybrid traits in large-scale populations. In preliminary steps, the pipeline extracts local features from omics data via convolutional neural networks, then employs graph convolutional networks to integrate these single-omics features with hybrid shared-parent graph (HSPG)

documents.title: Native Mass Spectrometry of Membrane Protein Lipid and Ligand Complexes Using de novo Designed WRAP Domains.
documents.abstract: Membrane proteins engage in dynamic transient interactions with surrounding lipids along with their substrates. Capturing these concomitant contacts often remains a challenging problem. Here, we demonstrate that generative deep learning-designed WRAP domains can preserve weak interactions of membrane proteins in native mass spectrometry. Using WRAP-fused GlpG, AqpM, and OmpA as model systems, we show that lipids can bind in multiple positions inside the WRAP, allowing for their characterization by native mass spectrometry. We show that lipid interactions can be altered by changing the WRAP str
documents.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

documents.title: Multicenter CT-Based Deep Learning for Preoperative Nodal Risk Stratification in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
documents.abstract: Accurate preoperative risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains difficult. We developed and validated ThyLNT, a Transformer-based 2.5D deep learning model using preoperative computed tomography (CT), and explored related biological features in multi-omics analyses.
documents.journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association

documents.title: Integrated Whole-Cell Phage Display and Machine Learning Identify Candidate Targeting Ligands in KRAS-Defined Lung Cancer Contexts.
documents.abstract: Phage display can identify ligands that target distinctive cell surface phenotypes, but selection outputs are often complex and difficult to interpret. Here, we developed an integrated workflow combining phage display biopanning, next-generation sequencing (NGS), machine learning (ML), and flow cytometry to discover short peptide binders associated with genotype-defined cancer contexts. Phage display was performed on lung cancer cell lines representing KRAS wild-type (WT), G12C, G12D, and G12V backgrounds, and experimental outputs were used to train a multimodal probabilistic model. From the r

documents.title: Large Language Model-Enhanced MFSSG Enables Effective and Accurate Integration Analysis for Microbiome-Metabolome Data.
documents.abstract: The massive volume of paired microbiome and metabolome measurementsgenerated through high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometryhas created an urgent need for dedicated, integrative analytical pipelines. Existing tools lack the capacity to simultaneously support sample clustering, multi-omics visualization, disease risk stratification, and biological age quantification using matched dual-modal datasets. To overcome this analytical bottleneck, we introduce the matrix factorization with shared and specific graph learning (MFSSG) toolkit: an unsupervised matrix factorization framework that

documents.title: An EFHD1-associated ADSC niche modulates treatment response in experimental models of ER-positive breast cancer.
documents.abstract: Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) modulate the breast cancer (BC) microenvironment, but their role in endocrine therapy resistance and clinical outcomes remains ill-defined.

documents.title: A dendritic cell-related prognostic signature in glioma: A multi-omic framework integrating transcriptomics, single-cell profiling, and clinical validation.
documents.abstract: Dendritic cells (DCs) infiltrating the glioma microenvironment can promote antitumor immunity or contribute to immunosuppression and immune escape. This dual role underscores the need to define dendritic cell-related genes (DCRGs) for prognostic assessment. Using transcriptomic and clinical data from glioma cohorts (The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA)), combined with scRNA-seq analysis, we identified ten pivotal DCRGs (CASP1, CD300LF, CTSB, GPR132, HLA-DQA1, PLCB2, RAC2, SIGLEC9, STAT6, TLR1) associated with patient outcomes. A DCRG-based risk signature, devel

documents.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc.
documents.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important cha
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Viro-BERT: Whole-genome attention for robust viral pathogen classification from next-generation sequencing data.
documents.abstract: Classifying viral pathogens from next-generation sequencing (NGS) data is central to diagnosis and genomic surveillance. Most deep learning classifiers, however, read only a fixed window at the start of each genome, typically a few hundred to a few thousand base pairs, and so ignore more than 95% of the sequence of large DNA viruses such as monkeypox virus (MPV) and herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1). We refer to this problem as Truncation Blindness. Here we present Viro-BERT, which splits a complete genome into overlapping 512-token windows, encodes each window with a shared DistilBERT encoder, a

documents.title: Unsupervised Deep Learning for Cryo-EM/ET Particle Classification.
documents.abstract: Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is widely used to determine protein structures from purified samples. With cryogenic electron tomography (cryo-ET), it is possible to image thin sections of cells and directly visualize diverse proteins in their native environment. However, separating the massive mixture of different types of proteins inside cells remains challenging, especially without human intervention. In this work, we present an unsupervised deep learning framework for classifying cryo-EM/ET particle images that jointly optimizes for pose and structure through an autoencoder-based m
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Evo2VED: a database of DNA large language model-derived scores for variant interpretation.
documents.abstract: The Evo2 Variant Effect Database (Evo2VED; https://dnallmved.org/) is a publicly accessible resource cataloging precomputed Evo2-derived variant effect scores, defined as allelic score differences, for 6.48 million human variants common in the gnomAD non-Finnish European population. Evo2VED includes scores from the 7B and 40B models under three scoring schemes, alongside annotations of variant function, evolutionary constraint, allele age, and disease associations. It integrates genome-wide association study (GWAS) data from UK Biobank, FinnGen, and the Million Veteran Program. Three complemen

documents.title: sorAI - a suite of machine learning models to predict plant polyploidy from target capture data.
documents.abstract: Polyploidy is a persistent feature of land plant evolution, yet it is often difficult to determine the ploidy of individual plants. The growing abundance of target capture data and other high throughput sequence datasets across plant species has generated interest in methods to infer ploidy from these data. We leverage chromosome count data and target capture data from the GoFlag probe set in ferns to train new machine learning models to infer if a sample is from a diploid or polyploid genome.
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: LLM Representations Rival Traditional Predictors and Enhance Multimodal Prediction of APOE4 and Aβ-Burden.
documents.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, non-invasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-β (Aβ) burden using Cookie Theft picture-descriptions from two cohorts, including Hebrew- and English-speakers (IRAP, N=134; and WRAP, N=1,541). Aβ burden was classified across lowest-quartile, median, and highest-quartile cutoffs, capturing accumulation below conventional amyloid-positivity thresholds. We compared embeddings from pretrained large language models (LLMs) to standard cognit
documents.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

documents.title: Unraveling the genetic architecture of the human mammillary bodies.
documents.abstract: The mammillary bodies are a central component of the hippocampal-diencephalic-cingulate network that is critically involved in emotion processing and memory function, yet their genetic architecture remains unknown. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of mammillary body volume in 38,064 participants from the UK Biobank and replicated our findings in the Rhineland Study cohort (N = 4,860). Mammillary body and hypothalamic subregional volumes were derived from structural brain MRIs using FastSurfer-HypVINN, an established and validated deep learning-based segmentation tool. Univar
documents.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

documents.title: HMB-Net: Synergizing Latent Sequential Dynamics and Local Sequence Motifs for Robust RNA Methylation Prediction.
documents.abstract: Accurate site-level identification of RNA post-transcriptional modifications is essential for deciphering epitranscriptomic regulation. However, existing deep learning predictors typically rely on either convolutional filters with limited receptive fields or self-attention mechanisms with quadratic complexity, while parallel hybrid networks often struggle to coordinate global sequence context with local motif sensitivity. Here, we present HMB-Net, an interpretable hybrid framework that couples a Selective State Space Model (Mamba) with a deep Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) netw

documents.title: stem.MAP: Identification of cell-type-specific protein complexes in mammalian embryonic stem cells.
documents.abstract: Protein complexes carry out critical functions during development. Mapping cell-type-specific protein complexes in early embryogenesis is essential for uncovering the molecular mechanisms of embryonic development. We unfortunately currently lack a catalog of protein complexes specific for embryogenesis including embryonic stem cells. Here we develop a proteomics-based machine learning workflow to predict protein complexes present in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESC). Our method integrates data from a cell-type agnostic protein complex resource with co-fractionation mass spectrometry (CF-MS) ex
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Zero-Shot Protein-Ligand Binding Site Prediction from Protein Sequence and SMILES.
documents.abstract: Accurate identification of protein-ligand binding sites is critical for mechanistic biology and drug discovery, yet predictive performance varies substantially across ligand families and data-availability regimes. We present a systematic ligand-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for residue-level binding-site prediction across three settings: overrepresented ligands with abundant examples, underrepresented ligands with limited examples, and zero-shot ligands unseen during training. Using a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering, we evaluate a progressive three-s
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Protify: A Benchmarking Platform Revealing Task Dependence and Homology Leakage in Protein Language Model Evaluation.
documents.abstract: Protein Language Models (pLMs) have become essential tools for computational protein analysis, and the rapid proliferation of architectures, training objectives, and pretraining corpora has produced a diverse and expanding model landscape. Evaluation practices, however, remain fragmented: studies use different datasets, preprocessing pipelines, and reporting conventions, so results rarely transfer between publications. Here we introduce Protify, an open-source platform that standardizes pLM benchmarking across zero-shot, supervised, and transfer-learning settings through a unified, low-code in
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: A protein language model for domain, functional site, and variant effect prediction.
documents.abstract: Protein sequence databases are growing far faster than experimentally curated annotations, limiting functional interpretation of newly identified proteins and coding variants. We developed PALM, a protein annotation language model that jointly predicts domain and functional-site occurrence, while preserving overlapping and nested annotations through a soft-target objective. PALM integrates ESM2 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learned layer aggregation, and a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder. PALM was trained on ∼15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences spanning 17
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free enrichment reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence in malignant effusions.
documents.abstract: Malignant effusions are clinically accessible yet underutilized sources of metastatic tumor cells. However, abundant background immune cells complicate tumor cell isolation and molecular characterization. We integrate AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free tumor cell enrichment with genomic profiling to characterize phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions.
documents.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

documents.title: Synthetic MPRA perturbation supervision improves variant-effect prediction in sequence-to-function models.
documents.abstract: Deep learning sequence-to-function (S2F) models learn to predict functional readouts, such as gene expression, from genetic sequence. However, these models are trained predominantly on the reference genome and struggle to accurately predict the effect of genetic variation on gene expression. Massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) explore the direct impact of genetic variation on gene expression, but saturation-mutagenesis MPRAs that measure variant effects directly remain limited, thereby restricting their use for fine-tuning S2F models. In this work, we investigate fine-tuning Borzoi, a s
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Predicting single-molecule chromatin distribution from DNA sequence.
documents.abstract: Genome regulation unfolds through dynamic and stochastic single-molecule events. Deep learning models that read gene regulatory activities from DNA sequences have markedly advanced our ability to predict cell-population-level averages. However, they cannot capture the full spectrum of heterogeneity and dynamics at the single-molecule level, which directly reflect the underlying mechanisms of genome regulation. Here, we introduce a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) framework that directly models the entire probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states from DNA sequence alone. We u
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq.
documents.abstract: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-di
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Computational immunogenicity prediction for mRNA vaccines: benchmarks, bottlenecks, and the peptide-nucleotide gap.
documents.abstract: Computational prediction of T-cell epitopes has become indispensable to vaccine design, yet the field still relies on the assumption that how much of a given antigen is produced is fixed by its coding sequence. However, this is not the case with mRNA vaccines, i.e. the design of the mRNA template can vastly alter the quantity of the same protein produced. Codon usage, guanine-cytosine (GC) content, untranslated-region (UTR) design, and predicted secondary structure together define how fast the message is translated and how long it survives, and therefore how much antigen ever reaches the prese

documents.title: Transformer models in genomics: from sequence analysis to population genetics and biodiversity.
documents.abstract: Modern genomics and artificial intelligence converge at a breakthrough point with the emergence of transformer-based large language models for genomic analysis. This review examines how transformer-based models have advanced genomic sequence analysis through novel tokenization strategies, self-attention mechanisms, and pre-training/fine-tuning paradigms. Unlike prior broad surveys, we focus on three sub-areas of genomics where transformer architectures have had a substantive impact: sequence-level analysis, population-level genetics, including genetic imputation and genome-wide association ana

documents.title: Interaction-finder: automated literature-based discovery of biological entity associations with quote-level provenance.
documents.abstract: Identifying interactions between biological entities is a cornerstone of molecular research, but assembling such lists from the literature is slow and tedious. For many research questions, no curated database exists, leaving researchers to survey the relevant literature themselves. We present interaction-finder, a tool that automates this process: given a topic string and user-defined entity types, it discovers relevant literature through LLM-guided iterative search, extracts candidate associations from full-text articles, and produces a ranked list where every association is backed by quoted

documents.title: Leveraging amino acid embeddings for accurate translation efficiency prediction.
documents.abstract: Accurate prediction of translation efficiency from messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences is an important step toward mRNA sequence design. In recent years, the widespread adoption of high-resolution ribosome profiling techniques, such as Ribo-seq, has led to rapid accumulation of large-scale datasets that capture the relationship between mRNA sequences and translation efficiency. This progress has facilitated the development of machine-learning-based models for translation efficiency prediction. However, most existing approaches rely primarily on mRNA-derived features, such as codon usage frequency a

documents.title: EV Barcode: A Machine Learning Driven Web Resource for Predicting the Cellular Origin of Extracellular Vesicles From Protein and mRNA Cargo.
documents.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membranous particles secreted by most cell types into the extracellular space, carrying proteins, RNAs, metabolites, and lipids that reflect the physiological state of their cell of origin. Hence, EVs are considered as powerful resource of non-invasive biomarkers for disease diagnosis and prognosis. However, identifying the cellular source of EVs in complex biological samples including blood, urine and milk remains a major challenge, limiting clinical and biological insights. To address this, we developed EV Barcode (https://evbarcode.org/), an open-source web

documents.title: Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention.
documents.abstract: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction, identifying which residues of a protein form the interface when bound to a specific partner, remains a challenging task with significant implications for drug discovery and understanding of protein structure and function. Existing computational methods are limited by small training datasets, inconsistent redundancy filtering, and reliance on three-dimensional structural information at test time. Here we present a sequence-only, partner-specific protein-protein interface predictor called HandShake. It combines ProstT5, a protein language

documents.title: Transductive Learning From a Transformer Foundation Model Improves the Taxonomic Classification of eDNA Metabarcodes.
documents.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a powerful and cost-effective biodiversity monitoring tool, providing comprehensive and non-invasive taxonomic inventories. However, eDNA-based monitoring is strongly dependent on the completeness of genetic reference databases, which varies greatly among regions and taxa. Since completing gaps at the species level is unrealistic in the short term, an alternative is to infer coarser taxonomic assignments for sequences belonging to species not yet in reference databases. To address this challenge, we introduce BouillaBERT, a novel deep learning method tai

documents.title: An antigen-specific protein language model guides CDR optimization for antibody design.
documents.abstract: The capacity of an antibody to recognize and bind an antigen with high specificity and strength (i.e., its binding affinity) is a key determinant in the design and optimization of neutralizing antibodies against pathogenic targets. Here we introduce Ab-Affinity, a fine-tuned protein language model (PLM) that predicts the binding affinity of an antibody against a target peptide within the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Cross-validation results shows that Ab-Affinity outperforms other PLM-based affinity predictors when evaluated on a held-out validation and independent test sets. When integrated with

documents.title: A Transformers Analysis Pipeline (TrAP) to Evaluate LINE-1 RNA Sequence Content.
documents.abstract: LINE-1 RNA has emerged as a potential regulator of chromatin organization and gene expression, as well as a candidate readout of cellular and disease-associated states. Accurate measurement of LINE-1 transcript abundance is therefore important for evaluating its regulatory, biomarker, and potential therapeutic relevance. Measurement is challenging in short-read RNA sequencing because similar LINE-1 loci produce ambiguous, multi-mapping reads and LINE-1-associated signal can arise from passive as well as autonomous transcription. We developed the Transformers Analysis Pipeline (TrAP), an alignm

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Precision Nanomedicine: Bridging Delivery Barriers, Controlled Release, and Clinical Translation.
documents.abstract: Targeted drug delivery aims to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity, yet its clinical translation remains limited by the unpredictable in vivo behaviour of nanocarriers. Although a broad range of nanocarrier platforms-including lipid-, polymer-, protein-, inorganic- and biomimetic-based systems-can improve drug solubility, pharmacokinetics, lesion-site accumulation and controlled release, their performance is frequently constrained by heterogeneous disease biology, insufficient tissue penetration, premature clearance, immune recognition and manufacturing variability.

documents.title: Integrative multi-omics, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation reveal PFAS-associated immune-inflammatory signatures in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
documents.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants increasingly implicated in respiratory disorders. However, the systems-level connections among PFAS-associated molecular perturbations, immune dysregulation, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to prioritize candidate links between PFAS-associated target information and COPD-related transcriptional and inflammatory signatures.

documents.title: Physiological proxies of feed efficiency in pigs: exploring the predictive value of blood biochemical and hematological profiles.
documents.abstract: Developing strategies to improve feed efficiency can help the swine industry become more sustainable while meeting the worldwide demand for pork products, yet most commercial barns cannot practically calculate direct metrics of individual feed efficiency. Physiological indicators of metabolic pathways can serve as intermediate variables to predict performance outcomes and, therefore, as biomarkers of feed efficiency and other desirable production traits in growing pigs. This research aimed to assess the role of conventional blood parameters as proxies for performance outcomes and their predict

documents.title: Integrative ferroptosis-related bioinformatics identifies PPARγ as a therapeutic target of ursolic acid against inflammation and pathological osteogenesis in ankylosing spondylitis.
documents.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease characterized by persistent inflammation and aberrant new bone formation. Ferroptosis has increasingly been implicated in immune dysregulation and pathological bone remodeling; however, its molecular involvement in AS and its potential value for natural product discovery remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify ferroptosis-related molecular targets in AS, screen natural compounds targeting the key candidate, and validate their therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

documents.title: Medical-oriented multi-label diagnosis of twelve-lead ECG signals via disease-aware relational modeling and pathology-aware temporal evidence aggregation.
documents.abstract: Twelve-lead ECG signals are of great value in cardiovascular disease screening and assisted diagnosis, but their multi-label recognition process is simultaneously affected by cross-lead structural dependencies, disease label co-occurrence relationships, and the dispersed distribution of pathological evidence in long-sequence signals. To address these issues, this study proposes a deep learning model for twelve-lead ECG multi-label diagnosis. The model adopts a Transformer-Mamba hybrid structure as the temporal encoding backbone to extract local waveform variations and long-range rhythm feature

documents.title: Machine learning prediction of 1-year thrombosis risk in membranous nephropathy: integration of renal pathology and early longitudinal trajectories.
documents.abstract: Patients with membranous nephropathy (MN) have an increased risk of thrombotic events. Existing prediction approaches primarily use clinical and laboratory measurements obtained at a single time point and rarely incorporate renal pathology or early longitudinal changes. This study integrated multiple types of information to predict the occurrence of thrombosis from 4 weeks after discharge to 1 year after being diagnosed with MN.

documents.title: A machine learning-assisted hypoxia-associated prognostic model reveals PFKP-mediated glycolytic regulation in uveal melanoma.
documents.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is a highly aggressive intraocular malignancy with strong metastatic propensity and poor response to immunotherapy. Hypoxia profoundly reshapes the tumor microenvironment and drives immune evasion. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-assisted hypoxia-related prognostic model and identify relevant metabolic candidates associated with UM progression.

documents.title: Predicting Translation Readthrough from Sequence Features in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
documents.abstract: Understanding translation readthrough in eukaryotes is fundamental for elucidating transcript evolution, deciphering gene expression codes, and advancing biotechnological applications. In this study, we present the first comprehensive analysis of the transcript features that determine readthrough efficiency in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. To predict readthrough efficiency, we engineered a set of novel sequence-derived features and trained multiple machine learning models, achieving a mean Spearman correlation of 0.535 between predicted and experimentally measured values, substantially improving p

documents.title: Prediction of multi-stage Alzheimer's disease progression based on surface-based morphometry and machine learning.
documents.abstract: Early identification of individuals at high risk of progression from normal cognition (NC) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and from MCI to Alzheimer's disease (AD) is crucial for timely intervention. However, predictive models that simultaneously address multiple transition stages along the AD continuum remain limited.

documents.title: Explainable volumetric deep learning from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI for preoperative IDH prediction in adult-type diffuse gliomas: a two-center study.
documents.abstract: To evaluate contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI (CE-T1WI) models for preoperative prediction of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status in adult-type diffuse gliomas and explore phenotype associations of influential latent features.

documents.title: Macronutrient composition and incident hypertension during China's nutrition transition: a longitudinal cohort analysis of the China Health and Nutrition Survey.
documents.abstract: China's nutrition transition has shifted dietary macronutrient composition while hypertension prevalence has risen. Whether the routinely available macronutrient composition adequately captures the risk of incident hypertension remains unclear.

documents.title: ToxiFusion: integrating contextual and compositional sequence representations for toxic peptide prediction.
documents.abstract: Accurately predicting of toxic peptides from sequence information is important for peptide safety assessment and therapeutic development. However, reported performance of computational predictors can be affected by representation limitations and evaluation bias.
